chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
For a man, at the time of his death, is one-third of his wealth, and if he did not make a will, it is not incumbent upon the heirs to validate it.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the one-third of an estate that can be bequeathed if no will is made?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the 'third' (thuluth) is a discretionary right of the testator rather than an obligatory debt, meaning heirs are not compelled to honor it if the deceased failed to explicitly bequeath it. This ruling distinguishes the voluntary bequest from fixed inheritance shares, emphasizing the autonomy of the deceased in allocating up to one-third of their estate to non-heirs or specific purposes.
